history.summary: ISKCON Juhu - the Sri Sri Radha Rasabihari Temple on four acres known as Hare Krishna Land - was founded by A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, founder of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness, and is ISKCON's flagship Mumbai temple. Prabhupada first envisioned the site in August 1965, a few weeks before leaving for America, when he passed a neglected four-acre plot near Juhu Beach. It took thirteen years - including six years battling a crooked landlord, his agents, and corrupt municipal officials - for the vision to be realised. Prabhupada spent 554 days in Bombay between 1971 and 1977, more than anywhere else, and in 1972 appointed his disciple Giriraj das Brahmachari (later Giriraj Swami) to lead the Juhu project. On Makar Sankranti, 14 January 1978, two months after Prabhupada's passing, his disciples inaugurated the white-marble temple with domes over a hundred feet high. It now draws millions of visitors a year and is one of the most internationally significant centres of the global Hare Krishna movement.

name: ISKCON Temple
town_description: Mumbai, the capital of Maharashtra and India's financial capital. The temple complex is at Juhu Church Road, Juhu, a beachside suburb of north-west Mumbai that was remote and undeveloped when the temple land was acquired in the early 1970s.

travel.airport: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (~8-10 km).
travel.railway: Vile Parle (Western line) is the nearest railway station (~3 km); Andheri station is also close.
travel.road: Well connected by road along Juhu Church Road; local buses, autos, and taxis serve the area. The complex includes a twin-towered seven-storey guest house.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami and Makar Sankranti are the biggest celebrations.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily 4:30 AM to 9:00 PM; closed 1:00 PM - 4:00 PM. Mangala Arati at 4:30 AM; Prabhupada's quarters open 5:30 PM - 8:30 PM. Entry is free for daily darshan; Govinda's Restaurant on-site serves sattvic vegetarian food.
